corrections.text: The article says a commit was counted as tagged "if a line of its message begins with 'Assisted-by:'" and gives 1,258 tagged commits for the 7.3 merge window, 3,008 for the 7.4 merge window and 1,877 through 7.3-rc7 ("seven fewer than LWN's 1,884"). Counting only lines that begin exactly with "Assisted-by:" gives 1,257, 3,007 and 1,876 (eight fewer than LWN's figure); the published numbers also matched an indented example line in the documentation commit 816d9992d9ed and one commit that writes "Assisted-By:". The shares at one decimal and the 105 of 913 for rc1 to rc2 are unchanged.

The article quotes LWN's "a strong consensus in the room" for dropping the tag. The removal commit describes it as "a strong, though not unanimous, consensus", and LWN reports that "Khan said that she still found Assisted-by to be useful".
